entries.label_vi: Dạy nghề ở trường → vào việc làm ổn định, đáp ứng thiếu hụt nhân lực, hiểu mình hợp nghề gì
entries.claim: Vocational training prepares pupils for the working world.
entries.because: Employers in construction, healthcare, engineering and hospitality report shortages of practically skilled workers, and pupils with such skills move into stable jobs more easily.
entries.result: Lower youth unemployment and earlier discovery of suitable careers.
entries.reuse_vi: Dùng cho đề giáo dục nghề, học nghề, học việc, thất nghiệp thanh niên.

entries.label_vi: Môn thực hành giữ chân học sinh không hợp học thuật; rèn nhóm, quản lý thời gian
entries.claim: Practical subjects keep engaged the pupils who find purely academic lessons discouraging.
entries.because: Students who struggle with written exams often thrive when they can build, repair or cook something tangible.
entries.result: Confidence is restored and the risk of dropping out falls.
entries.rebuttal: They must not replace literacy and numeracy, and pupils should not be directed towards trades too early.
entries.reuse_vi: Dùng cho đề nghệ thuật, thể thao, dạy nghề, giảm bỏ học.

entries.label_vi: Giáo dục tài chính → tránh nợ xấu và bị lừa (thẻ tín dụng, vay online, lãi suất)
entries.claim: Understanding money helps people to avoid debt and exploitation.
entries.because: Credit cards, student loans and online lending make borrowing easy, but interest, fees and long-term consequences are hard to understand.
entries.result: Pupils who learn how interest works and compare offers are less likely to be misled or overwhelmed by debt.
entries.reuse_vi: Dùng cho đề môn tài chính, quản lý tiền, nợ sinh viên.

entries.label_vi: Học lập ngân sách / tiết kiệm sớm → an toàn tài chính khi trưởng thành, ít phụ thuộc phúc lợi
entries.claim: Early lessons in budgeting and saving shape lifelong habits.
entries.because: Children who plan a monthly budget, set savings goals and tell needs from wants build financial security as adults.
entries.result: Less stress and dependence on welfare, and support for goals such as buying a home or starting a business.
entries.reuse_vi: Dùng cho đề kỹ năng sống, môn mới trong trường, hướng nghiệp.

entries.label_vi: Dạy đạo đức → biết lập luận về đúng sai thay vì chỉ theo luật
entries.claim: Ethics lessons teach children to reason about moral questions instead of merely following rules.
entries.because: Discussing real dilemmas, such as reporting a cheating friend or behaving online, trains pupils to weigh evidence, consider other perspectives and justify decisions.
entries.result: Independent judgement helps them resist peer pressure and tempting shortcuts.
entries.reuse_vi: Dùng cho đề dạy đạo đức, công dân, tôn giáo, tư duy phản biện.

entries.label_vi: Giáo dục đạo đức → khoan dung, công dân có trách nhiệm; trường bổ sung cho gia đình
entries.claim: Ethics education promotes tolerance and responsible citizenship.
entries.because: Classrooms bring together children of different cultures and beliefs, and structured discussion teaches them to listen to views they do not share.
entries.result: Less prejudice, more cooperation and safer communities.
entries.rebuttal: Families differ and many children receive little guidance at home; schools can offer a neutral setting to complement them.
entries.reuse_vi: Dùng cho đề công dân, đa văn hoá, tôn giáo, giáo dục giá trị.

entries.label_vi: Dạy phòng chống tội phạm → hiểu hậu quả, chống áp lực bạn bè, rẻ hơn xử lý sau
entries.claim: Teaching young people the consequences of crime helps to prevent it.
entries.because: Lessons on peer pressure, drug misuse, online fraud and cyberbullying give pupils the knowledge to resist risky situations; prevention is cheaper than policing and prisons.
entries.rebuttal: Lessons must be age-appropriate and only one part of a wider strategy.
entries.reuse_vi: Dùng cho đề an toàn, phòng chống tội phạm, an toàn mạng.

entries.label_vi: Giáo dục công dân → tham gia đời sống cộng đồng, bỏ phiếu, tình nguyện
entries.because: Pupils who learn how local government works, why voting matters and how to volunteer take part in community life as adults.
entries.reuse_vi: Dùng cho đề công dân, tình nguyện, hội đồng học sinh.

entries.label_vi: Phục vụ cộng đồng bắt buộc → đồng cảm, trách nhiệm, kỹ năng làm việc nhóm
entries.claim: Compulsory community service develops empathy and a sense of responsibility.
entries.because: Time with elderly residents, homeless people or children with disabilities makes social problems real, and pupils learn teamwork, communication and reliability.
entries.result: Qualities valued by employers and universities.
entries.reuse_vi: Dùng cho đề tình nguyện, thực tập, nghĩa vụ xã hội.

entries.label_vi: Cộng đồng được lợi từ nhân lực tình nguyện; phản bác 'ép buộc làm mất thiện chí'
entries.claim: Communities benefit from the extra help that compulsory service provides.
entries.because: Charities, hospitals and councils gain willing volunteers and projects such as clean-ups become possible.
entries.result: Many reluctant starters continue voluntarily once they see results; a requirement reaches all students, not only the motivated.
entries.rebuttal: Let pupils choose from a range of projects to limit resentment.
entries.reuse_vi: Dùng cho đề nghĩa vụ, quân dịch, dịch vụ cộng đồng bắt buộc.

entries.label_vi: Học VỀ các tôn giáo → hiểu văn hoá, lịch sử, thời sự; giảm định kiến
entries.claim: Learning about religions builds cultural understanding.
entries.because: Religious ideas shape art, literature, law and politics worldwide, and familiarity with other beliefs weakens stereotypes.
entries.result: Pupils understand history and current events better and respect neighbours' traditions.
entries.reuse_vi: Dùng cho đề tôn giáo, đa văn hoá, môn lịch sử.

entries.label_vi: Giới hạn: dạy trung lập, không truyền đạo; tôn trọng quyền của gia đình
entries.because: Beliefs are private and parents differ; a lesson that promotes one faith may clash with family wishes and amount to indoctrination.
entries.result: Teach about beliefs factually and neutrally, alongside non-religious worldviews, and let families opt out of devotional activities.
entries.reuse_vi: Câu giới hạn cho đề tôn giáo, đạo đức, giá trị.

entries.label_vi: Học sinh tham gia quản trị trường → trách nhiệm, kỹ năng dân chủ, quyết định thực tế hơn
entries.claim: Taking part in decision-making teaches responsibility and democratic skills.
entries.because: Pupils on school councils learn to listen, negotiate compromises and own the results, and they understand budgets and priorities; their insight improves decisions.
entries.result: A stronger sense of belonging and more respect for rules they helped to shape.
entries.reuse_vi: Dùng cho đề hội đồng học sinh, dân chủ trong trường, lãnh đạo học sinh.

entries.label_vi: Giới hạn: an toàn, nhân sự, chương trình cốt lõi vẫn do người lớn quyết
entries.because: Safeguarding, staff appointments and the core curriculum need professional expertise and legal responsibility.
entries.result: Student voice works best as consultation on appropriate issues, with adults keeping the final say.
entries.reuse_vi: Câu giới hạn cho đề trao quyền cho học sinh.

entries.label_vi: Quảng bá đa dạng văn hoá → giảm định kiến, kỹ năng thực tế cho thế giới toàn cầu
entries.claim: Promoting diversity broadens pupils' horizons and weakens prejudice.
entries.because: Celebrating different languages, festivals and histories teaches children to appreciate other traditions, a practical skill for working with colleagues from many countries.
entries.result: Differences seem interesting instead of threatening.
entries.reuse_vi: Dùng cho đề đa văn hoá, trao đổi văn hoá, ngoại ngữ, di cư.

entries.label_vi: Công nhận đa dạng → học sinh thiểu số thấy mình thuộc về, đi học đều, ít bị bắt nạt
entries.claim: Recognising diversity helps minority pupils to feel that they belong.
entries.because: Children who see their language, religion and history respected are more confident and engaged, whereas those who feel invisible may withdraw or face bullying.
entries.result: Better attendance, results and cooperation across groups.
entries.rebuttal: Promotion should not be tokenistic; it must appear in materials, staff training and everyday practice, and stress shared values.
entries.reuse_vi: Dùng cho đề đa dạng, hoà nhập, chống bắt nạt.

entries.text: A teenager who learns basic electrical installation at school, for example, may qualify for an apprenticeship at sixteen instead of drifting between short-term jobs.
A graduate who understands compound interest, for example, will think carefully before relying on a credit card to cover everyday expenses.
A student who has debated the fairness of sharing exam answers, for example, may be better prepared to resist the temptation to cheat.
A teenager who has learned how online scams work, for example, is far less likely to become a victim or an accomplice.
A teenager who helps to run a weekly food bank, for example, learns how much effort is needed to support people in need.
A class that studies how festivals such as Diwali, Ramadan and Christmas are celebrated, for example, learns respect for neighbours' traditions.
A student representative who helps to design a recycling scheme, for example, learns to present a proposal, gather support and manage a small project.
A school that invites parents to share cooking and stories from their home countries, for example, helps pupils to see differences as interesting instead of threatening.
